definitions.explanation: Having or appearing to have length, width, and depth. Used in science, technology, and everyday language.
In otaku culture, refers to the real world and real people, as opposed to the two-dimensional world of anime, manga, and games.

examples.japanese: {三次元|さんじげん}の{映像|えいぞう}を{楽|たの}しむ。
{三次元|さんじげん}プリンターで{模型|もけい}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a model with a 3D printer.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{三次元|さんじげん}{対応|たいおう}の{映画館|えいがかん}で{見|み}たほうがいい。
examples.english: You should see this movie at a theater that supports 3D.

examples.japanese: {三次元|さんじげん}には{興味|きょうみ}がない。
examples.english: I have no interest in the real world. (said by an anime fan)

examples.japanese: {二次元|にじげん}より{三次元|さんじげん}のほうが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I prefer real people to fictional characters.

examples.japanese: {三次元|さんじげん}の{女性|じょせい}にはまったく{興味|きょうみ}がないと{言|い}っていた。
examples.english: He said he has absolutely no interest in real women.

notes:
USAGE:
In technical contexts, refers to 3D space or 3D technology. In internet and otaku culture, {三次元|さんじげん} (3D, real world) contrasts with {二次元|にじげん} (2D, anime/manga world). This slang usage is widely understood in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三次元|さんじげん}プリンター (3D printer)
- {三次元|さんじげん}{映像|えいぞう} (3D imagery)
- {三次元|さんじげん}CG (3D computer graphics)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {二次元|にじげん}: two-dimensional, 2D — also used for the anime/manga world
- {立体|りったい}: solid, three-dimensional — more formal/technical synonym
